item.subject: science
item.stem:
Chetan compares three classroom samples: water, a liquid made when hydrogen and oxygen are chemically joined into a compound whose properties differ from those separate elements; a dish of iron filings mixed with sulphur powder that a magnet can still pull apart as a mixture; and a strip of pure copper metal, an element that looks like one single solid piece of metal.

Which claim correctly classifies water?

options.A: Water is a compound: hydrogen and oxygen are chemically joined, and water's properties differ from those of the separate elements.
options.B: Water is a mixture: it contains more than one element, just as iron filings mixed with sulphur powder do.
options.C: Water is an element: it looks like one single liquid, as copper looks like one solid piece of metal.
options.D: Water is a compound even though hydrogen and oxygen keep their own separate properties inside it.
